headline: Anthropic's Fable 5 beats Pokémon FireRed with vision-only harness, costing $65.40
summary: An independent replication of Anthropic's Fable 5 Pokémon run shows it can beat the first gym in 1,785 turns. However, a deeper look at its reasoning reveals a complex internal process.
details: Anthropic claimed its Fable 5 model could beat Pokémon FireRed using only visual input. An independent researcher replicated this claim, successfully earning the first gym badge in 1,785 turns at a cost of $65.40.

The researcher built a 'minimal, vision-only harness' to match Anthropic's described constraints, allowing Fable 5 to play the game. At the 2,000-turn limit, the model had a three-Pokémon team and was progressing through Route 3.

While the core claim of beating the first gym with visual input is verified, the 'thinking chains' revealed a more intricate process than initially suggested. The model was making complex decisions and recalling game details not visible on screen.

This finding challenges the perception of 'vision-only' capabilities in AI models. Many systems claiming similar feats often rely on reading data directly from the game's memory or using other forms of scaffolding.

Previous Claude models struggled with Pokémon FireRed even with extensive assistance. Fable 5's performance, while impressive, raises questions about the true extent of its independent visual reasoning versus its underlying architecture.

Academic benchmarks show that frontier models typically achieve very low completion rates on games like Pokémon when restricted to raw screenshots and button presses. This highlights the significant leap Anthropic claims Fable 5 has made.
